sources.quote: The alert hit social media around 9:34 a.m. ET on Tuesday, about seven hours after pseudonymous on-chain sleuth ZachXBT had identified an alleged North Korean hacker, Keisuke Watanabe, who reportedly worked as the CTO at Stabble last year.
It then admitted that it employed Watanabe a year ago.
The new team that recently acquired the protocol said it had discovered that a former CTO appeared to be the same person ZachXBT had publicly flagged as a North Korean IT worker.

notes: This is a source-triangulated media bridge, not independent government attribution or civil-identity verification. Decrypt, Protos, and CryptoSlate all rely materially on ZachXBT and Stabble's public sequence; the reviewed Stabble posts confirm an unnamed former DPRK developer but do not themselves name Keisuke.

sources.quote: The protocol, which was recently taken over by a new team, began the day with around $1.75 million in TVL, according to data from DeFiLlama. After publicly sounding the alarm to a potential emergency, that value is down to less than $663,000.

notes: Protocol-level point-in-time reporting only. It does not establish an exploit, asset loss, manipulation, personal causation, or responsibility by the persona; Stabble separately said no exploit had occurred.
